_doc: THE MODEL TABLE. One place, public, in the repository (V2-500, operator's rule 2026-08-30).
This used to live in SIX places that drifted apart in silence: config/v2.py::_DEFAULTS,
nucleo/flash/provider_chain.py, nucleo/workers/providers.py, voice/engine/core/config.py,
engine/fly.accounts.toml and cloud/provisioner/src/machineConfig.js. Nothing compared any of them, so the
rule ended up living in the operator's LOCAL config — which is gitignored and does not travel — and every
fresh install, and the cloud, booted with something else. It surfaced when the cluster brain spent Z.AI
credits nobody had authorised: the internal catalogue was headed by Z.AI and no file in the repo said so.
RULES THAT GOVERN THIS TABLE (all of them the operator's):
1. A titular, ONE stand-in, and AT MOST a third rung (reiterated 2026-09-10). Never more than three
levels anywhere — a fourth cannot be reasoned about, configured or debugged; if you find one, trim it.
2. DeepSeek through its DIRECT provider is the titular of everything that is not the Brain Worker or a
MEMORY service. The memory services (heart, REM, embeddings) run on OpenAI DIRECT as titular
(operator directive 2026-09-10 — supersedes the 2026-08-21 no-OpenAI removal, for memory only).
3. AIMLAPI is failover ONLY — second or third rung at most, NEVER the titular of any service.
4. Z.AI belongs to the Brain Worker ONLY, inside Claude Code. It is nobody else's failover (V2-496).
5. Everything here has to be able to run IN THE CLOUD. Ollama cannot: it is a local server and inside a
container it does not exist. That is why the embeddings go through a CLOUD provider (measured — see
that row).
THESE ARE THE DEFAULTS, not the effective configuration. The user changes them from the frontend's settings
panel (store `config/v2.json`, gitignored): other providers, their own keys. Whatever they write there WINS
over this file, and this file is what someone who has changed nothing gets.
THE KEYS ARE NOT HERE. This holds the NAME of the variable (`key_env`); the value is resolved from the
credential store by endpoint. This file is public.

voice_brain.label: FlashBrain — the voice and chat turn
voice_brain.why: V4.1-Flash, promoted by the operator 2026-09-22 — and it is a RETURN to Flash, which is where voice belongs: «la voz es algo que tiene que funcionar súper ágil». v4-pro took the seat on 2026-08-15 for routing (41/42 vs 38/42) and the price was reasoning latency. MEASURED 2026-09-22 against his own key: `deepseek-flash` SEES images (a red square → «Rojo», 1.77 s — the release's headline capability, live), while `deepseek-v4-pro` returned an EMPTY body in 7.47 s on the same call, spending a 400-token budget on reasoning. ⚠️ THE ID IS `deepseek-flash`: /models lists only that and `deepseek-v4-pro`, and `deepseek-v4.1-flash` answers 400 «The supported API model names are…». An announcement is not a model — measured twice now. ⚠️ OPEN RISK, stated plainly: the 2026-08-15 bench measured the OLD Flash failing `show widget` 3 of 3. 4.1 is a different model and has NOT been re-benched; the operator promoted it knowing that, and the re-bench is owed.
voice_brain.failover_why: OpenAI `gpt-4.1-mini` — the ONE stand-in, chosen by the operator 2026-09-22 after every native candidate was probed against his real keys that day: xAI 403 (credits gone, confirming the 2026-08-30 retirement), Groq 403 (code 1010), Mistral 429 (free-tier rate limit), Gemini 2.5-flash 200/1.6 s but ANSWERED IN PORTUGUESE to a Spanish prompt on the first probe. `gpt-4.1-mini` answered 200 in 1.16 s in correct Spanish and its tool-calling is already proven in this engine. His standing preference: NATIVE providers, never a broker — «hay más posibilidades de que se caiga IML que que se caiga el proveedor original». ⚠️ TWO RULES GOVERN EVERY ROW BELOW. (1) A stand-in may never SHARE A PROVIDER with its titular — the old latency relay got this wrong, it also pointed at `api.deepseek.com`, so a DeepSeek outage took both rungs and the ladder was decorative. (2) OPENAI IS NEVER A TITULAR (operator, 2026-09-22): «OpenAI siempre tiene que ser failover; tenemos modelos baratos como titulares, los más potentes a nuestra disposición».

brain_worker.label: Brain Worker / SlowBrain — the one that browses and executes
brain_worker.why: Driven by the Claude Code CLI, which speaks the ANTHROPIC protocol — that is why both endpoints are `/anthropic`, and why Z.AI's credits wallet (`paas/v4`, OpenAI-compatible) CANNOT be used here. `vision:false` is measured: the GLMs and DeepSeek V4 confabulate about images they cannot see, so the browser works off the DOM.

brief_composer.label: Brief composer — steers the worker's search
brief_composer.why: Asks for the answer, not the deliberation (`no_thinking`). If the model CANNOT turn reasoning off, it retries WITH reasoning and a 3200 budget (V2-488) — before that, every directed search ran blind, in silence.
brief_composer.failover_why: OpenAI `gpt-4.1-mini` — the ONE stand-in, same choice and same two rules as §voice_brain (operator, 2026-09-22).

memory_writer.label: Memory · HEART — distils every turn into pills
memory_writer.why: ⚠️ INVERTED 2026-09-22 by the operator, and it reverses his own 2026-09-10 directive that put OpenAI at the head of the memory services. The new rule is general and beats it: «OpenAI siempre tiene que ser failover; tenemos modelos baratos como titulares, los más potentes a nuestra disposición». The two models simply swap seats — nothing else about this service changes, and `gpt-4.1-mini` is still one call away when DeepSeek is down. OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-10: the memory services (heart, REM, embeddings) run on OpenAI DIRECT as titular — this supersedes the 2026-08-21 no-OpenAI removal FOR MEMORY ONLY. gpt-4.1-mini is not a new bet: the 2026-08-09 sweep (21 candidates x 34 cases x 4 axes) scored it top-tier on the two axes that destroy data, and it was this seat's rung until 2026-08-21. Measured live before this switch (2026-09-10): 200 on chat/completions with the house key. gpt-4o-mini remains VETOED here (puts an English-stated allergy into slot=operator.diet). Writes off the hot path, so latency costs nothing.
memory_writer.failover_why: OpenAI `gpt-4.1-mini`, demoted from titular to stand-in on 2026-09-22 — see §why. Same rules as §voice_brain.

memory_rem.label: Memory · REM sleep — nightly synthesis and repair
memory_rem.why: ⚠️ INVERTED 2026-09-22 by the operator, and it reverses his own 2026-09-10 directive that put OpenAI at the head of the memory services. The new rule is general and beats it: «OpenAI siempre tiene que ser failover; tenemos modelos baratos como titulares, los más potentes a nuestra disposición». The two models simply swap seats — nothing else about this service changes, and `gpt-4.1-mini` is still one call away when DeepSeek is down. The same model as the HEART on purpose: they write to the same place with the same judgement. §12.2 measured gpt-4.1-mini at 100% on THIS task. Operator directive 2026-09-10: memory services run on OpenAI DIRECT as titular.
memory_rem.failover_why: OpenAI `gpt-4.1-mini`, demoted from titular to stand-in on 2026-09-22 — see §why. Same rules as §voice_brain.

embeddings.label: Memory · embeddings (the semantic space)
embeddings.why: ⚠️ THE ONE ROW THE «OpenAI IS NEVER A TITULAR» RULE (operator, 2026-09-22) CANNOT REACH, and it is not an oversight. An embedding model DEFINES the vector space every pill in `zaelar.db` already lives in: swapping it does not change a provider, it invalidates the whole stored memory, because vectors from two models are not comparable. Moving it is a MIGRATION — re-embed everything, then switch — never a config edit. Flagged for the operator; nothing here changed. CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT on 2026-08-29 (12 facts ES+EN, 12 queries sharing NO words with their fact, recall@1): text-embedding-3-small 12/12 margin +0.204 · mistral-embed 10/12 +0.050 · fastembed bge-small 7/12 +0.021 (an ENGLISH-ONLY model: on Spanish it misses one in three). DeepSeek has NO embeddings endpoint (404 verified) and AIMLAPI's returns 403, so there is no provider choice to make here. 768 dims are requested via the `dimensions` parameter (matryoshka): it measures the same as 1536 (12/12, +0.204 vs +0.201) and fits the `EMBED_DIM` the database already has — changing the model does NOT force a schema migration. Ollama is OUT by the operator's rule: it is a local server and inside a container it does not exist.
embeddings.warning: NO FAILOVER, DELIBERATELY: a second provider is ANOTHER vector space, not a stand-in — mixing them is the defect that cost V2-482/484/485. If the provider falls, the vector is DEFERRED (the writer marks `embed_pending`, REM repairs it) and recall drops to lexical, said in amber; the space is never swapped in flight. Changing this value changes the SPACE: the signature lives in `<db>.embedsig` and migrating requires `memory/reembed.py`.

reranker.label: Memory · reranker
reranker.why: OFF by default so LOCAL and CLOUD measure the same thing. Its model (jina-reranker, ~1.1GB) downloads on first boot and dominated a Machine's cold start (2min18s -> 58s with it off), so the cloud has run without it since 2026-08-13; shipping it on by default locally meant measuring locally a system that does not exist in the cloud. It is an ORDERING improvement, not a source: without it recall still works, just worse ordered. Turn it on with `local` (fastembed on CPU) from the panel once the memory grows.

stt.label: Voice · STT (speech to text)
stt.why: Both are cloud services and serve a container. Local Whisper is out by the same rule as Ollama.

tts.label: Voice · TTS (text to speech)
tts.why: Operator, 2026-09-26: Inworld first, ElevenLabs second. Measured through the engine's own LiveKit plugins (V2-774): inworld-tts-2 first audio 185/168 ms (es/en) vs 194/175 for eleven_turbo_v2_5, at half the price ($25 vs ~$50 per 1M chars). The model is chosen by the builder (`voice/engine/speech/tts/inworld.py`, env ZAELAR_INWORLD_TTS_MODEL) and billed per CHARACTER by `energy_tariffs`, not per token, so it is not named here. Cartesia was ruled out on cost and Kokoro is local.
tts.failover_why: ElevenLabs stays selectable in the panel and is the documented second. There is NO automatic TTS failover in the engine today: if Inworld runs out of balance the voice stops, and that has to be VISIBLE in the panel, not guessed — switch the panel to ElevenLabs.

triage.label: Messaging · triage of what arrives
triage.why: It used to be xAI `grok`, which on 2026-08-30 returns 403 for EXHAUSTED CREDITS — and grok is vetoed for routing on measured mis-routing. Out.
triage.failover_why: OpenAI `gpt-4.1-mini` — the ONE stand-in, same choice and same two rules as §voice_brain (operator, 2026-09-22).

susurro.label: Susurro — proactive background suggestions
susurro.why: OFF by default after the Susurro->worker loop incident that drowned the voice. Turned on from the panel — the operator's own install has had it on since 2026-07-26, once the circuit breaker existed.
susurro.failover_why: OpenAI `gpt-4.1-mini` — the ONE stand-in, same choice and same two rules as §voice_brain (operator, 2026-09-22).

retired._: What was removed and WHY, so nobody adds it back believing it is missing.
retired.xai: Credits exhausted (403 verified 2026-08-30) and `grok` vetoed for routing on measured mis-routing.
retired.groq: The model we had declared (`llama-3.3-70b-versatile`) NO LONGER EXISTS: 404 `model_not_found`. A rung with an expired name is worse than no rung.
retired.ollama: A local server: inside a container it does not exist. Operator's rule — everything in this table has to be able to run in the cloud.
retired.cartesia: Ruled out by the operator on cost.
retired.zai_credits: Z.AI's pay-per-use wallet (`paas/v4`) is OpenAI-compatible and the worker speaks Anthropic, so it cannot use it; and outside the worker Z.AI is not used at all (V2-496).
